about.title: About
about.body1: DollarsOut is a companion to 1STAND's economic-pressure action list. The idea is simple: individual spending decisions feel too small to matter, so most people never make them. Counted together, they stop feeling small.
about.body2: Every action here is something you can actually do — cancel a subscription, move an account, walk away from a platform. You log the ones you've done, and the collective total goes up for everyone watching.
about.body3: The action list is a first-pass draft maintained here, not a live feed from anywhere else. Nothing you do in this app touches any other 1STAND system.
about.privacyBody: We store your email address and which actions you've logged. That's it — no name, no tracking, no selling, ever. The public ledger shows what was done and when, never who did it. You can export or delete everything in two taps from Account.
help.title: Help
help.q1: How does logging an action work?
help.a1: Find an action, tap "I did this". That's the whole thing — one tap, no forms, no amounts to enter. It counts toward your own progress and toward the collective total on the home screen.
help.q2: Why do I have to sign in?
help.a2: So the count means something. Without an account, one person could log the same action a thousand times. Signing in is an email address and a one-time code — no password to create or remember.
help.a3: Every action logged by everyone this month, against the monthly goal. The needle sweeps from zero on the left to the goal on the right, and it resets at the start of each month.
help.q4: Can other people see what I did?
help.a4: Not as you. The public ledger lists the action and a timestamp, with no account attached — so "Cancelled Amazon Prime · 4m ago" is visible, but never who did it. Your own list is yours alone.
help.q5: I made a mistake — can I undo it?
help.a5: Yes. Right after logging one, tap Undo in the banner that appears. New accounts also don't count toward the public totals for the first 48 hours, which keeps the collective number honest.
